items.title: Anthropic's Fable 5.2 completes 41 percent of real freelance jobs, up from 2.5 percent a year ago
items.content_text: Anthropic's Fable 5.2 model has achieved a 41.3% success rate on the Remote Labor Index, completing professional freelance projects at a standard acceptable to paying clients. This represents a 16-fold increase in capability since the benchmark's inception a year ago, signaling a massive leap in agentic productivity.

items.title: Evolving metal extraction processes
items.content_text: The metals industry has experienced transformational moments before: the Bessemer process, flash smelting, electric arc furnaces, and modern continuous casting all changed what was possible. Yet, for more than a century, most extraction processes rely on techniques and pathways that would be familiar to metallurgists from generations ago. Processes have become larger and control systems smarter, but the fundamental science behind separating metals from ores has changed less than many realize.

items.title: Sources: Microsoft is among a group of companies lobbying the Trump administration to halt the FCC's plan to ban imports of Chinese optical transceivers (Alexandra Alper/Reuters)
items.content_text: Microsoft is actively lobbying the Trump administration, alongside other tech giants, to block the FCC's proposed ban on Chinese optical transceiver imports. Given the massive reliance of data centers on cost-effective optical components, Microsoft aims to secure supply chain stability and prevent a surge in infrastructure construction costs.

items.title: Anthropic kicks off IPO roadshow, offering shares at $70 to $78 and targeting a trillion-dollar valuation
items.content_text: Anthropic is launching its IPO to go public on Nasdaq, offering 825 million shares while securing a $26 billion private placement from major tech giants. The company is targeting a trillion-dollar valuation to cement its position as a top-tier rival to OpenAI.

items.title: Filing: Anthropic's IPO could give it an up to $1.405T valuation on a fully diluted basis, up from the $965B valuation during its $65B Series H announced in May (Ashley Capoot/CNBC)
items.content_text: Anthropic said it will offer 825 million shares in its upcoming IPO at a price range between $70 to $78 per share, according to an updated filing on Tuesday, bringing the five-year-old artificial intelligence lab a step closer to a potentially historic Nasdaq debut. At the high end of the range, Anthropic would net up to $64.35 billion in proceeds through the IPO. items.title: Sources: Jensen Huang and Alice Huang's relationship dates back to at least 2023, facilitating $7.5B+ in Nvidia chip shipments via Chinese companies since then (The Information)
items.content_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Alice Huang have been linked since 2023, with reports suggesting this connection facilitated over $7.5 billion in Nvidia chip shipments to China. This relationship has emerged as a potential bypass for export restrictions, raising serious concerns regarding regulatory compliance.

items.title: BT CEO Allison Kirkby says a Starlink deal is "ready to launch" but the company is "cautious on how Starlink might be viewed" after the Ukraine service cutoff (Kieran Smith/Financial Times)
items.content_text: BT CEO Allison Kirkby stated that a deal with Starlink is ready, but the company is delaying the launch due to concerns over brand reputation following the service cutoff in Ukraine. This highlights the conflict between operational expansion and geopolitical risks for telecom giants partnering with Musk.

items.title: Anthropic's Fable 5.2 represents "Jagged AGI" that matches human expert levels on select tasks like game design, but lacks self-directed judgment and taste (Ethan Mollick/One Useful Thing)
items.content_text: Anthropic has released the Claude Fable 5.2 model, which matches human expert-level performance in complex intellectual tasks like game design. However, it still lacks independent judgment and aesthetic taste, representing what is categorized as 'Jagged AGI'.

items.title: Tear Down Those Guardrails! Meet the Renegades Freeing Chatbots From Corporate Enslavers
items.content_text: Former Apple engineer Thomas founded Abliteration AI, a venture focused on removing safety guardrails from open-weight models and making them accessible to the public. The initiative aims to challenge the industry narrative that equates uncensored models solely with illicit activity.

items.title: The AI Safety Debate Has Lost the Plot. We Asked 10 Experts What the Real Nightmares Are
items.content_text: Addressing the rising 'AI doom' narrative, a panel of experts has scrutinized industry rhetoric, finding the fear of human extinction largely hyperbolic. The industry is urged to move beyond alarmist discourse to focus on defining and managing realistic technical risks.

items.title: China's trade surplus hit $1.04T in the first 10 months of 2026, topping $1T for a second year in a row, as AI-driven tech exports offset weak domestic demand (Reuters)
items.content_text: China's trade surplus reached $1.04 trillion in the first 10 months of 2026, marking a historic scale. This growth is primarily driven by surging demand for AI-related tech exports, effectively offsetting the downturn pressure from weak domestic consumption.
